edges.effect_quant: Pooled meta-analytic evidence suggest a small average effect that is directionally consistent but not dramatic.
edges.mechanism: Ultraviolet exposure can directly induce DNA photoproducts and mutational damage in skin while also modifying vitamin D status and immune surveillance. For Melanoma, the critical issue is usually cumulative and intermittent UV patterning rather than simply time spent outdoors.
edges.summary: Pooled meta-analytic evidence link sunlight / uv exposure to higher risk of melanoma in light-skinned adults. The average effect is usually small rather than dramatic, so this edge is better read as a risk modifier than a stand-alone cause or cure.
edges.caveats: Dose, timing, and baseline risk still matter. Observational edges may partly reflect broader lifestyle patterning, while small trials can overstate benefit if follow-up is short.
